name: Name tag: hooked arrow
when: A character is named while on screen. The plate sits lower, off to one side (shoulder height), and a thin hooked arrow rises from it and turns in to the head. Good when the space beside the face is busy but there is room lower down.
anchor: The scene starts on the character's name: the hook draws from frame 3, its head bites on frame 9, the name types out from frame 11 (the plate's frames).

vars.theme: clean or vice: the video's theme
vars.name: the character's name as the voice says it (shown in capitals), 20 characters at most
vars.role: one short line about them, 40 characters at most; empty = the plate stays one row, name only
vars.headX: the head point, x in px on the 1920x1080 frame: the outer edge of the head (hair or ear) at eye level, on the side the plate goes; with side = below, the bottom of the chin. Read it off a snapshot of the shot; 60 px off still reads right
vars.headY: the head point, y in px
vars.side: right or left: the plate 100 px out and 96 px below the point, the hook rising from it and turning in at eye level; below: the plate 120 px under the chin and off to the side, the hook leaving its near edge and turning up into the chin
vars.out: seconds after the start: when it starts to leave (the scene ends 0.23 s later)

changed: nametag-A with its face box replaced by a curved arrow (5 px stroke) from the plate to one head point; the plate moves down to shoulder height. The arrow's head bites in with the brackets' lock-on motion; the plate's frames are nametag-A's. The role line is full white at weight 500 (was 74 % white).
